Assuming Postgres and a `users` table (swap in your own names). I have not run this against a database.

```sql
-- migrate: split users.full_name into first_name / last_name
BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE users
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

-- ponytail: first word = first name, everything after = last name.
-- Wrong for "Mary Ann Smith" style names; fix those by hand, no heuristic gets names right.
-- ponytail: single UPDATE; batch by id range if the table is large enough for lock time to matter.
UPDATE users
SET first_name = substring(btrim(full_name) from '^\S+'),
    last_name  = substring(btrim(full_name) from '^\S+\s+(.*)$')
WHERE first_name IS NULL
  AND last_name  IS NULL
  AND full_name  IS NOT NULL;

COMMIT;
```

It is safe to run twice because `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op the second time, and the `WHERE` clause only touches rows that are still unsplit. A re-run will not overwrite names that were edited after the first run.

Single-word names such as "Cher" get `first_name = 'Cher'` and `last_name = NULL`.

To check the result, this should return 0:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM users
WHERE btrim(full_name) <> '' AND first_name IS NULL;
```

Skipped: dropping `full_name`. Do that in a separate migration (`ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS full_name;`) once the app no longer reads or writes it, because it is irreversible and this backfill needs the column to re-run.
